text: Use when a landing page targets a named account, contact, selected account group or audience segment, or when adapting a campaign across 1:1, 1:few and 1:many modes.

Keep seller identity/capabilities, target identity, target facts, audience/task hypotheses, campaign intent and relationship evidence separate. A name and logo establish identity; they do not establish needs, stack, results or endorsement.

Read [audience modes] to choose the actual unit of relevance: one account/contact, an evidenced segment, or a shared audience. Event and regular landing pages follow their own offer. Do not default any mode to a pilot.

Join a supported seller capability to the supplied audience's task. Without target research, write an invitation or proposed use. Remove the name/logo mentally: the remaining argument must still explain the task relevance.
Record which evidence changed the section choice, emphasis or proof; when nothing beyond identity changed, report that level honestly.
Preserve actual derivation markers, bound identity and version lineage through the existing tools. … Report concept, template and derived artifact status separately.
note: legacy template/derivation mechanics; the site agent has no derivation.

text: Contact-level facts require strong identity binding AND an appropriate allowed use. Public availability is not permission to turn private interests or sensitive traits into outreach. Missing support means omitting the facet, never inventing one.
note: Site: "Never name people at the account"; the site workspace carries no contact research.
